Inphinit Proxy

Validation

The Validator is a data validation class that helps minimize the amount of code you need to write.

Experimental: This is an experimental feature being considered for inclusion and may be subject to change or refactoring

Validating

Validating POST:

use Inphinit\Experimental\Utility\Validator; $validator = Validator::post(); $validator->field('name', $name, 'required|min:5|max:15|regex:/^\S+$/'); $validator->field('surname', $surname, 'min:5|max:50'); // strings such as yes, true, and 1 return bool(true) // strings such as no, false, and 0 return bool(false) // Other values return null $validator->field('active', $active, 'required|bool'); if ($validator->valid()) { echo 'Name: ', htmlentities($name); if ($surname !== null) { echo ' ', htmlentities($surname); } echo '<br>'; echo $active ? '✔️' : '❌'; } else { foreach ($validator->failures() as $failure) { echo '<div class="error"><p>', $failure, '</p></div>'; } }

Validating GET:

use Inphinit\Experimental\Utility\Validator; $validator = Validator::get(); $validator->field('query', $query, 'min:5'); $validator->field('type', $type, 'in:electronics,motors,fashion,sports'); $validator->field('sold', $sold, 'bool'); if ($validator->valid()) { ... }

Validating Arrays and JSONs.

use Inphinit\Experimental\Utility\Validator; $arr = [ 'foo' => '...', ]; $validator = new Validator($arr); $validator->field('foo', $phone, 'required|regex:/^(?:55)?([1-9]{2})(9?[2-9]\d{3}\d{4})$/'); if ($validator->valid()) { ... }
use Inphinit\Http\Request; use Inphinit\Experimental\Utility\Validator; $app->action('POST', '/receive', function () { $body = file_get_contents('php://input'); if (strlen($body) < 1) { Request::status(400); return 'Invalid request'; } $decoded = json_decode($body, true); if (json_last_error() !== JSON_ERROR_NONE || is_array($body) === false) { Request::status(400); return 'Invalid body'; } $validator = new Validator($decoded); ... });

Validation Rules

Before validation, the values are converted to a string:

Rule Combinations Description
bool Can be combined with in and required String values such as yes, true, 1, no, false, and 0
decimal Can be combined with in, regex, min, max, and required Validates that the field contains a decimal number string. The separator can be set using: decimal:., decimal:,, decimal:'
digit Can be combined with in, regex, min, max, and required Validates that the field contains a string written as an integer
email Can be combined with in, regex, min, max, and required Validates an email address using FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL
in: Can be combined with in, regex, min, max, and required Checks if the field's value is one of the values in the provided list; example: in:foo,bar,baz
ip Can be combined with in, regex, min, max, and required Validates an IP address using FILTER_VALIDATE_IP
max:<n> If used with decimal or digit, it compares directly against the field's value: field <= max; for other rules, it compares against the number of characters: strlen(field) <= max
min:<n> If used with decimal or digit, it compares directly against the field's value: field >= min; for other rules, it will compare against the number of characters: strlen(field) >= min
regex:<n> Validates the field using a custom regular expression, example: regex:/^[A-Z]+$/
required Can be combined with all rules Makes the field mandatory
url Can be combined with in, regex, min, max, and required Validates a URL using FILTER_VALIDATE_URL and checks if the scheme is https or http

Customizing the messages

By default, error messages are in English, but it is possible to modify them and configure them to work with any language system you choose to use, such as Gettext.

The first %s contains the field name or path. As for messages that contain more than one %s, the explanations follow:

Message Default Note
bool %s can have values such as Yes, True, 1, No, False, and 0
decimal %s expects a decimal format
digit %s expects a digit format
email %s expects a valid email
in %s has an unexpected value
ip %s expects a valid IP
max %s expects a maximum %s of %s The second %s represents the type, and the third represents the maximum value.
min %s expects a minimum %s of %s The second %s represents the type, and the third represents the minimum value.
regex %s does not match the expected format
required %s is required
type %s contains an unexpected type
unicode_error %s contains invalid Unicode characters This is not part of the validation process, however, in cases where a field contains problematic characters, this is handled as one of the failures, rather than as an exception, to prevent the system from breaking
url %s expects a valid url

Example of customization using gettext:

$validator = Validator::post(); $validator->setMessage('bool', _('boolId')); $validator->setMessage('decimal', _('decimalId')); $validator->setMessage('digit', _('digitId')); $validator->setMessage('email', _('emailId')); $validator->setMessage('in', _('inId')); $validator->setMessage('ip', _('ipId')); $validator->setMessage('max', _('maxId')); $validator->setMessage('min', _('minId')); $validator->setMessage('regex', _('regexId')); $validator->setMessage('required', _('requiredId')); $validator->setMessage('type', _('typeId')); $validator->setMessage('unicode_error', _('unicode_errorId')); $validator->setMessage('url', _('urlId'));

The .po file should contain something like:

msgid "boolId" msgstr "O valor deve ser yes ou no." msgid "decimalId" msgstr "O valor deve ser um número decimal."
